Let’s dive into Chapter 8—Sustaining Innovation: Adapting to Changing Jobs.
You know, while the core needs of customers usually stay the same, the world around them never stops changing. Things like the economy, new tech, or even shifting social trends can completely reshape what progress looks like for people—and the way they want to achieve it.
So, how do organizations keep up and stay innovative? Well, it really comes down to three big habits.
First, always be listening for new and emerging jobs. This means getting close to your customers, watching how they live, and picking up on those fresh struggles or wishes that pop up. The more tuned in you are, the earlier you’ll spot those subtle shifts.
Second, don’t be afraid to experiment—even if it means shaking up your own business model. Sometimes, the smartest move is to disrupt yourself before someone else does. It’s all about trying new solutions, even if they challenge the way things have always been done.
And third, build feedback loops right into every step of your customer’s journey. Quick, low-risk experiments—like pilot programs or limited releases—let your team learn fast and adapt even faster. That way, you’re never stuck waiting for the “perfect” answer; you’re always moving, always evolving.
Here’s a helpful way to picture it: think of innovation not as building a rigid, unmoving structure, but more like gardening. You’re cultivating something living—an ecosystem that grows, changes, and sometimes needs a little pruning. It’s about patience, attention, and being willing to let go of what no longer helps your customers.
Just imagine a streaming service that notices viewers are starting to use its content to unwind after tough days, not just for entertainment. Instead of sticking to old formulas, the service could roll out mood-based playlists or even guided relaxation sessions. By doing this, they stay right in step with the evolving jobs their customers are hiring them for.
So, the big idea here? Sustaining innovation isn’t about locking in the perfect solution—it’s about staying curious, flexible, and ready to adapt as your customers’ lives change.
